Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:10:2.hebrew: לקטלא - לישא עליו חטא. ועל עצמו היה אומר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:10:2.english: To death - To bear sin upon himself. And he would say [this] about himself.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:10:3.english: And he does not do the needs of his house - He does not attend to the needs of his household here.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:10:4.english: And he enters his home empty-handed - For he earns nothing here.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:10:5.hebrew: ולואי שתהא ביאה - שאחזור לביתי, כיציאה שיצאתי מביתי בלא חטא — שלא אטעה ואענש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:10:5.english: And if only [the] entry will be - That I should return to my home like the departure when I left my home without sin, so that I do not err and be punished.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:11:1.english: A convoy - A group of people.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:11:2.hebrew: אם יעלה לשמים וגו' - כדי שלא תזוח דעתו עליו, היה אומר כך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:11:2.english: Though [his excellency] mount up to the heavens, etc. - In order that he would not become arrogant, he would say this.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:11:3.english: Like his own dung - [The word] galal [means] dung.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:11:4.hebrew: מכתפי להו - נושאין אותן על הכתף, שהיו זקינים ואינם יכולין לרוץ, ומטריחין את הציבור לעמוד בפניהם. לפיכך, היו עבדיהם נושאין אותם מהר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:11:4.english: Carried them on [their] shoulders - They would carry them on the shoulder, for they were elderly and unable to walk quickly, and [would otherwise] burden the congregation to stand before them. Therefore, their servants would carry them quickly.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:11:5.hebrew: בשבתא דרגלא - שבת ששואלין בו בהלכות הרגל, והיינו שלשים יום קודם הרגל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:11:5.english: On the Shabbat of the Festival - The Shabbat on which they inquire into the laws of the Festival, and that is thirty days before the Festival.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:12:1.hebrew: מתונים - רגילין בהמתנה, כדי לעיין בה יפה קודם שתחתכוהו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:12:1.english: Deliberate - Accustomed to waiting, in order to examine it thoroughly before you decide it.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:12:2.english: By steps - Forcefully and in haste.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:12:3.hebrew: על ראשי עם קדש - שכשהיה המתורגמן דורש, היו הציבור יושבין לארץ; והמפסיע ביניהן לילך ולישב במקומו, נראה כמפסיע על ראשן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:12:3.english: Over the heads of the sacred nation - For when the interpreter [meturgeman] was expounding, the public would sit on the ground; and one who strides between them to go and sit in his place appears as though he is stepping over their heads.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:12:4.english: And juxtaposed to it: “Now these are the ordinances” - That is to say: I am warning the judges as well.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:13:1.hebrew: כלי הדיינים - דשייכא בהו שימה, דבר המטלטל:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:13:1.english: The judges’ tools - For [the term] “setting” is applicable to them, [as they are] a movable object:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:13:3.hebrew: מקל - למכת מרדות, עד שיחזור בו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:13:3.english: A rod - For lashes of rebellion, until he relents.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:13:4.english: A shofar - For excommunication and a ban.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:14:1.hebrew: ואצוה - כל צואה לשון זירוז הוא, דתניא (קדושין דף כט:): כל מקום שנאמר צו אינו אלא לשון זירוז. ועל מה זירז? על המקל ועל הרצועה, שיהו מטילין אימה על הציבור לשם שמים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:14:1.english: And I charged - Every command is an expression of urging, as it is taught (Kiddushin 29b): Wherever it is stated “Command,” it is nothing other than an expression of urging. And regarding what did he urge [them]? Regarding the rod and regarding the strap, that they should cast awe upon the community for the sake of Heaven.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:14:2.hebrew: שמוע בין אחיכם - כשיהיו שניהם יחד, שמעו דבריהם, ולא תשמעו דברי זה בלא זה, שמסדר דברי שקר כדברי אמת לפי שאין מכחישן; ומכיון שלב הדיין נוטה לו לזכות, שוב אין לבו מהפך בזכות השני כל כך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:14:2.english: Hear [the causes] between your brethren - When both of them are together, hear their words, and do not hear the words of this one without that one; for he arranges false words like true words, since there is no one to contradict them, and once the heart of the judge inclines toward him in his favor, his heart will no longer search for the merit of the second [litigant] as much.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:14:3.hebrew: שמע - דבריך בין אחיכם — כשתהיו שניכם יחד משמע:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:14:3.english: Make heard - [Make] your words [heard] between your brethren — [which] implies when the two of you are together.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:15:1.hebrew: לא תשא - לא תקבל שמע שוא — אזהרה לדיין; וקרי ביה נמי: "לא תשיא" — אזהרה לבעל דין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:15:1.english: You shall not bear - You shall not accept a false report — [this is] a warning to the judge; and also read into it: “You shall not cause [another] to bear” — [this is] a warning to the litigant.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:16:1.hebrew: בין איש ובין אחיו - שנפלה להם בית בירושה, אל תאמר: טול אתה בית ואחיך עליה, ומה בכך? הרי לכל אחד יש לו דירה! אלא העלה אותן בדמים, והשווה חלוקתן ע"י מעות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:16:1.english: Between a man and his brother - Where a house fell to them as an inheritance, do not say: “You take the house and your brother the upper story, and what of it? Behold, each one has a residence!” Rather, assess them in value and equalize their division by means of money.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:17:1.hebrew: בין גרו - לשון מגור, תשמישי דירה. אל תאמר: יטול זה תנור וזה כירה, שהרי תנור עודף על הכירה, וצריך להוסיף דמים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:17:1.english: “And between his stranger” - [This is] an expression of dwelling [magor], [referring to] household articles. Do not say: Let this one take an oven and that one [take] a stove, for an oven exceeds a stove [in value], and [he] must add money.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:18:1.english: Do not recognize him - If he is your friend.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:18:2.hebrew: לא תנכרהו - אם הוא שונאך, לא תעשה לו כנכרי לחייבו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:18:2.english: Do not estrange him - If he is your enemy, do not treat him like a stranger to find him liable.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:19:1.english: He said to him - That man [said] to Rav.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:19:2.hebrew: ולאו אושפיזכני את - כלומר, אין אתה זכור שעשיתי עמך חסד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:19:2.english: “And are you not my guest?” - That is to say: Do you not remember that I did a kindness for you?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:19:4.english: That man said to him: I have a legal case - And I want you to be [the] judge.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:1:1.english: The bed of Solomon - The dwelling place of the Omnipresent.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:1:2.hebrew: ששים גבורים - תלמידי חכמים, וששים לאו דוקא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:1:2.english: Sixty mighty men - [These are] Torah scholars; and "sixty" is not exact.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:1:3.english: Expert in war - The battle of Torah.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:2:1.english: If it is clear to you - The judgment [is clear] like the morning, which shines.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:2:2.hebrew: אומרהו - והכי משמע: דינו לבקר — הוציאו לאור משפט:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:2:2.english: State it - And this is what it means: “Execute justice in the morning” — bring justice forth to light.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:3:1.english: A collar hangs - The punishment for perverting [justice].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:3:2.hebrew: לתלמיד היושב לפני רבו - ובא דין לפני רבו, והוא לא נזקק לדבר — נענש אם שתק, והוא מבין ברבו שטועה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:3:2.english: To a student who is sitting before his teacher - And [where] a case came before his teacher, and he was not called upon to deal with the matter — he is punished if he remained silent while he realized that his teacher was erring.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:4:1.hebrew: דנמטיין שיבא מכשורא - שיגיענו נסורת קטנה מן הקורה. כלומר, שאם נטעה — ישתלש העונש בין כולנו, ויקלו מעלי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:4:1.english: So that a splinter from a beam will reach us - That a small splinter from the beam will reach us. That is to say, if we err, the punishment will be divided among all of us, and [the burden] will be lightened for me.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:4:2.hebrew: שיבא - נסורת, כמו (הושע ח׳:ו׳) כי שבבים יהיה עגל שומרון, ומתרגמינן: לניסרי לווחין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:4:2.english: A splinter - Sawdust, as in (Hosea 8:6): “For the calf of Samaria shall be splinters,” and we translate [it in the Targum]: “Into shavings of boards.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:4:3.english: The butchers - [They are] experts in tereifot.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:5:1.hebrew: אם דומה הדיין למלך - שבקי בטיב דינין ומלא חכמה, כמלך זה שהוא עשיר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:5:1.english: If the judge is like a king - That he is expert in the nature of legal rulings and full of wisdom, like this king who is wealthy.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:5:2.hebrew: שמחזר על הגרנות - לשאול תרומותיו, ואף זה צריך לחזר לשאול ב"ד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:5:2.english: Who goes around to the threshing floors - To ask for his terumah gifts; and this [judge] too needs to go around to ask the court:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:6:1.english: Stand over him as an interpreter - To announce to the public the lecture that he will whisper to you.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:7:1.hebrew: וה' בהיכל קדשו - סמוך להאי קרא דהוי אומר לעץ הקיצה, עורה לאבן וגו', הוא יורה, הנה הוא תפוש וגו', כתב: "הס מפניו כל הארץ" — יכלה על עון הזה את כל הארץ:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:7:1.english: And the Lord is in His holy Sanctuary - Adjacent to this verse, “Woe to him who says to the wood: Awake; arise to the stone, etc., can this teach? Behold, it is overlaid, etc.,” [Scripture] wrote: “Let all the earth be silent before Him” — He will destroy all the earth on account of this sin.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:8:1.hebrew: כל עץ - משמע דיין, דכתיב (דברים כג): "כי האדם עץ השדה", ומוקמינן ליה בתלמיד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:8:1.english: Any tree - This implies a judge, as it is written (Deuteronomy 23): “For man is a tree of the field,” and we establish it as referring to a Torah scholar.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:8:2.hebrew: אצל מזבח - ות"ח מכפרין ומגינין כמזבח:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:8:2.english: Beside the altar - And Torah scholars atone and protect like the altar.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:9:1.hebrew: אלוה הבא בשביל כסף - דיין שהעמידוהו ע"י שנתן ממון למלך על כך:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 7b:9:1.english: A judge who comes due to silver - A judge whom they appointed because he gave money to the king for this.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 7b:14:1.hebrew: תהא זריז - שלא להטיל אימה על הציבור לרדותם יותר מדאי. וכן מוכח לקמן (סנהדרין דף ח.), דדרשינן מהאי קרא: אזהרה לדיין שיסבול את הציבור:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 7b:14:1.english: "Be vigilant" - Meaning, not to cast fear upon the community so as to subjugate them excessively. And so it is proven later (Sanhedrin 8a), as we derive from this verse: A warning to a judge that he must bear the burden of the community.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 7b:5:1.hebrew: שאינו צריך לכלום - כלומר, דגמיר וסביר. וכן מוכח מדמייתי עלה: "דבי נשיאה אוקמו דיינא דלא גמיר". ומיהו בפי"ג דכתובות (דף קה:) מייתי לה על דיין שאינו מקבל שוחד, ומשמע שאין צריך לכלום — שהוא עשיר:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 7b:5:1.english: "That he does not need anything" - That is to say, that he is learned and possesses analytical understanding. And so it is proven from [the fact] that [the Gemara] cites in connection with this: "In the house of the Nasi, they appointed a judge who was not learned." However, in chapter 13 of Ketubot (105b), [the Gemara] cites it regarding a judge who does not accept bribes, which implies that "he does not need anything" [means] that he is wealthy.
